interest: For a historian, this single-entry docket sheet illustrates U.S. diplomatic surveillance of Japanese relations and migration policy in Latin America and the Caribbean during the interwar period. It demonstrates American vigilance regarding potential concessions granted to Japanese subjects in bilateral agreements with Cuba, capturing explicit assurances that existing domestic immigration restrictions remained unaltered. Furthermore, the cross-reference to decimal file 637.9431/4 provides a valuable archival trail directing researchers to substantive records on Cuban-Japanese commercial and diplomatic negotiations.
overview: This file consists of a single-page State Department 'List of Papers' docket sheet for decimal file 894.5537, titled 'Immigration Into Japan from Cuba.' It records a single incoming despatch (Cuba Despatch No. 192 from diplomat Reed, dated May 2) concerning immigration provisions within an agreement between Cuba and Japan. The docket notes assurances provided by Mr. Ortiz that the agreement conferred no new rights or privileges upon Japanese subjects beyond those already granted by existing legislation, and refers researchers to file 637.9431/4 for related correspondence.

subfiles.summary: This document is a State Department 'List of Papers' docket sheet indexing records under decimal file 894.5537 relating to immigration into Japan from Cuba. It catalogues Despatch No. 192 sent from Cuba by diplomat Reed on May 2 regarding immigration privileges under a Cuba-Japan agreement. The note records assurances by Mr. Ortiz that the agreement does not grant Japanese subjects any rights beyond existing legislation, and cross-references file 637.9431/4.
